issues.body:
Verified at the PR head, docs/branch-protection.md:13-14 (§Protected branch, untouched by this diff) still reads:

    - **`main`** — the only long-lived branch. All changes land via pull request; direct
      pushes are disallowed (including for administrators — see "Other settings").

The rewritten §Other settings (lines 426-430) now says the live ruleset carries a repository-role bypass actor with `bypass_mode: always` — i.e. an administrator CAN bypass. The stale sentence does not merely coexist with the correction: it names §Other settings as its own supporting evidence, so a reader following the pointer lands directly on the refutation.

This round did fix three other instances of the same overclaim inside this file (line 540 "Trusted committer only" row, lines 521-526 Scorecard paragraph, line 561 live-ruleset preamble), which makes the remaining one harder to excuse as an oversight of scope — it is the headline claim of the document's first substantive section, and removing exactly this overclaim is the PR's entire purpose. For a compliance doc-of-record an internally contradictory record is worse than a uniformly wrong one: neither statement can be relied on.
issues.fix_hint: Update docs/branch-protection.md:13-14 to match §Other settings, e.g.: "All changes land via pull request; direct pushes are disallowed for non-administrators. Repository administrators retain an always-on ruleset bypass (see §Other settings) — the automated landing flow does not use it." Then re-grep the file for any remaining unqualified enforcement-is-uniform wording (`grep -n 'administrator\|uniform\|bypass' docs/branch-protection.md`) before landing.

issues.body:
Verified stale at the PR head — the compliance artifacts an auditor actually reads still assert precisely the claim this PR retracts:

- compliance/openssf/controls/openssf.md:26 — Branch-Protection control, evidence string ends "... block force-push/deletion, no bypass actors."
- compliance/slsa/controls.md:141 — SL-S-b, "`docs/branch-protection.md` records the *required* ruleset: … no-admin-bypass …"
- compliance/slsa/controls.md:142 — SL-S-c, "`docs/branch-protection.md` (… block branch deletion, no admin bypass)"
- compliance/slsa/evidence.md:125 — Two-person review (AR), "`docs/branch-protection.md` (… no admin bypass)"

After this PR those four claims are false in the audit-facing direction (asserting a protection that is not enforced), and they cannot be caught by re-reading the source doc because the source doc no longer says what they quote. This PR touches gap-register.md — the very file where a weakened control is supposed to be recorded — yet the GX-OSSF-3 edit only swaps "no-bypass" for "merge-queue" in the compensating-controls list and does not register the resulting gap or fix the four dependents.

This also violates the source file's own rule at docs/branch-protection.md:576-578: update "this table and the matching section above in the same commit so the doc-of-record never lags the live ruleset." The spirit of that rule — no lagging record of the ruleset — extends to the compliance docs that quote it.

(Filed against compliance/openssf/gap-register.md because the schema requires a path present in the diff and that is where the gap belongs; the evidence-string edits are in the three files listed above.)
issues.fix_hint: In this same PR: (1) replace "no bypass actors" / "no admin bypass" / "no-admin-bypass" in the four locations with the honest form, e.g. "repository-administrator bypass present (`bypass_mode: always`); the automated landing path does not use it and remains constrained by merge-queue admission, squash-only, no force-push, no deletion"; (2) if OpenSSF Branch-Protection or SLSA SL-S-c is thereby no longer fully satisfied, add a row/note to compliance/openssf/gap-register.md rather than restating the weakened claim as met. Pre-existing drift worth fixing while in those files: compliance/slsa/controls.md:141 and compliance/slsa/evidence.md:125 also still claim "≥1 approving review, require-code-owners, dismiss-stale", which docs/branch-protection.md:521-524 records as 0/false/false. Also note research/orchestration-private-registry-worker.md:257 repeats "no bypass".

issues.body:
Unchanged from round 1 and now widened. docs/branch-protection.md:426 heads the item "**Repository administrators have an emergency bypass.**" while the value recorded one line later is `bypass_mode: always`. GitHub's bypass modes are `always` and `pull_request`; there is no "emergency"/break-glass mode, and `always` encodes no situational limit at all. "Emergency" implies a control (invoked only under a declared exception) that the configuration does not implement — the same class of soft overclaim this PR exists to remove.

This round propagated the wording rather than tightening it: docs/branch-protection.md:526 now says "Repository administrators retain the explicit emergency bypass documented above", and compliance/openssf/gap-register.md GX-OSSF-3 now says "with the administrator emergency bypass stated explicitly" — so the unsupported qualifier is now also in an auditor-facing compliance register. The body prose at 428-430 remains honest ("an explicit exception to uniform enforcement, not a compensating control"), and line 540 uses the accurate "can always bypass" — so the file is now inconsistent with itself on this word too.

Smaller, related: the prose infers "repository administrators" from `actor_id: 5` without recording the role name the API returns; recording the resolved role makes the next reconciliation mechanical.
issues.fix_hint: Drop "emergency" in all three places (docs/branch-protection.md:426, :526, compliance/openssf/gap-register.md GX-OSSF-3) in favour of what the config supports — e.g. "Repository administrators can always bypass the ruleset (`bypass_mode: always`)". If break-glass-only use is intended, state it as a *policy* line explicitly distinguished from the enforced setting ("policy: used only for declared incidents; not enforced by the ruleset"). Optionally record the resolved role name from `gh api …/rulesets/<id>` next to `actor_id: 5`.
issues.title: "emergency bypass" still overstates the recorded constraint (`bypass_mode: always`), and the wording has now spread to two more locations

issues.body:
.github/workflows/bench.yml:378 ("the `main` ruleset (id 17688455: … EMPTY bypass list) rejects it with `GH013`"), bench.yml:447 ("direct pushes to main are blocked, empty bypass list"), and .github/workflows/bead-autoclose.yml:36 ("GH013, empty bypass list — confirmed on the first real run") all assert the state this PR retracts.

The empirical conclusion is still correct — the default GITHUB_TOKEN / github-actions bot is not a repository administrator, so it is rejected whether or not an admin bypass actor exists — but the stated *reason* is now wrong, and bench.yml:394 proposes "Option A — add the github-actions bot to the `main` ruleset bypass list" while describing that list as empty. A future reader reconciling the ruleset hits the same contradiction this PR is resolving elsewhere.

No behavioural effect; comments only, and those files are outside this diff (filed against a diff path per schema).
issues.fix_hint: Amend the three comments to say the bypass list contains only the repository-administrator role (no bot/app actors), so the GH013 rejection of GITHUB_TOKEN stands for the right reason. Fold into this PR or file a follow-up `self-improvement` issue.

verdict.summary:
Doc-only change retracting the false "empty bypass_actors / current_user_can_bypass: never" claim and recording the live state (repository-role bypass actor, actor_id: 5, bypass_mode: always) plus a merge_queue row in the live-rules table. Round 2 extends the correction into three more places carrying the same overclaim — the "Trusted committer only" row (540), the solo-maintainer paragraph (521-526), the live-ruleset preamble (561) — and updates GX-OSSF-3 in gap-register.md. Real collateral progress; direction remains honesty-improving. I could not verify the live ruleset (no gh/API access), so its values are taken at face value — safe, since the claim is being weakened.

BOTH round-1 majors remain unfixed at the PR head, verified against the checkout:

1. docs/branch-protection.md:13-14 still reads "direct pushes are disallowed (including for administrators — see 'Other settings')", and that cross-reference points at the section this PR rewrote to say the opposite. The doc contradicts itself self-referentially in its first substantive section — and this round fixed three other instances of the same overclaim in the same file, so the omission is not a scope boundary.

2. Downstream compliance artifacts still cite this doc for the retracted claim: compliance/openssf/controls/openssf.md:26 ("no bypass actors"), compliance/slsa/controls.md:141 ("no-admin-bypass") and :142, compliance/slsa/evidence.md:125 ("no admin bypass"). False in the audit-facing direction; the source file's own drift rule (576-578) requires doc and dependents move in the same commit. This PR edits gap-register.md — where the resulting gap belongs — without registering it.

The round-1 minor persists and WIDENED: "emergency bypass" is unsupported by bypass_mode: always, and now also appears at :526 and in the gap-register cell. The "EMPTY bypass list" workflow nit is unchanged.

Same findings at the same severities as round 1 → stagnant. No code, tests, or security surface touched.
